dedupe_keys.name: inclusive public space project pedestrian participant interview dataset ips dataset 1

description: This dataset holds interviews with pedestrians who meet accessibility barriers in streets, collected by the Inclusive Public Space project (Law, Universality and Difference in the Accessibility of Streets), a European Research Council Advanced Grant project from 2019 to 2025 led at the University of Leeds by Anna Lawson. Participants were disabled people, older people and others such as parents with young children, in two cities in each of five countries: Delhi and Pune in India, Nairobi and Mombasa in Kenya, Almere and Utrecht in the Netherlands, Glasgow and Leeds in the United Kingdom, and Syracuse and Atlanta in the United States. They reflected on what they found problematic about the design, condition or use of streets, its impact on their lives, and their experience of complaints and legal enforcement. Coverage: ten cities in five countries. Access: published in Research Data Leeds in 2026; data collection and analysis documentation is open, while the interviews are held in the Restricted Access Data Repository (RADAR) and require a request form, with a first response within 10 working days. Licence: documentation CC BY 4.0; interview access on request; free. Caveats: qualitative data. Simulation uses: accessibility barriers for inclusive street design and pedestrian models. Related records: the Montreal 3-30-300 indicator and JuPedSim.
